newsitem.title: UK: Kenwood shareholders reject sale resolution.
newsitem.headline: Kenwood shareholders reject sale resolution.

text.p: Kenwood Appliances Plc said on Monday that shareholders voted against a resolution that would require the company to talk to third parties with the aim of soliciting a bid.
It said shareholders representing 60.8 percent of the issued share capital lodged proxies on the resolution. Of these, 81.9 percent voted against with 18.1 percent for.

Kenwood said in a statement following today's extraordinary general meeting that it will consider any serious and credible proposals put forward which may result in an offer for the company, "if they provide the prospect of enhancing shareholder value."
Last week, Pifco Holdings Plc said that Kenwood had rejected two of its recent proposals which called for a merger of the two companies.
Kenwood confirmed that the company was approached by Pifco, but added that it never received a formal bid.
Today's meeting followed recent moves by rebel shareholders led by Brian Myerson and Julian Treger and their UK Active Value group aimed at selling the group.
